builderInsights.title: Boris Cherny
builderInsights.suggestedSummary:
Also today: Claude Docs, Claude Slides, and Claude Design are in every conversation.

Ask Claude for a presentation and you get one you can open, edit, and export as PowerPoint or PDF. Same for a document or a design. There's no separate tool to navigate to. They're just in the chat.

Claude Code showed that AI could do real work, not just answer questions. Developers hand Claude a feature, come back to shipped code. That's where much of the industry's serious engineering runs now.

Cowork proved knowledge workers could do the same: hand Claude the brief, come back to finished files.

Today, chat and Cowork start merging into one Claude. The direction: one Claude that carries context across everything you're working on, wherever you are. Simple enough for everyone to access Claude's full capabilities.

I've been using this experience every day for the last few weeks, and it feels awesome. Simpler, faster, and more powerful.

We're rolling this out slowly. We'll be fine-tuning the experience as we go to ensure it is fast and reliable. Can't wait to hear what you think.

builderInsights.title: Cat Wu
builderInsights.suggestedSummary:
Today, we are merging Claude Cowork and chat to simplify how you use Claude!

We are also integrating Claude Design so that you can ask Claude to make a Slide, Design, or Doc without needing to switch tabs or apps.

Many of you shared that you didn't want to choose which Claude product to use for any task. As Claude models have become more capable, we've found that Claude can handle the routing for you. Based on your prompt, Claude will decide whether to give a quick answer or do deeper agentic work, and what kind of output best fits the task.
 
You're in control the whole time: you can still stop, redirect, or exert finer control over Claude's effort or approach.
 
Give it a try and let us know what you think. We're rolling this out slowly over the next few weeks to get it right.

builderInsights.title: Aaron Levie
builderInsights.suggestedSummary:
Incredibly exciting that there are entire universes of AI innovation that still exist that weren’t even on most of our radars.

Being able to process information insanely quickly, at crazy low costs, with high levels of capability is huge for a wide number of enterprise tasks.

Data classification tasks, routing decisions inside of a workflow, decision making when handed a particular domain problem, quick judgment calls about safety or security, and more all are the gates in a large number of  processes. 

This model and approach could be quite cool in agentic workflows in the enterprise.

builderInsights.title: Thariq
builderInsights.suggestedSummary:
I think Claude Managed Agents strikes the right balance here, the sandbox is optional and can be spun up independently of the rest of the agent loop.

I recently ported an old project that was focused on bash tool calling to CMA and it worked well!

I think increasingly you can just give Claude tools shaped in the way you want vs tricking it with a layer of indirection

e.g. for data storage do you really want a file system or do you want an API to a database

this is again, an update to me from last year

related to this- I think bash is no longer all you need, if your goal is just reliably tool calling

but sandboxes + bash are still good for work that involves code generation & execution https://t.co/xTptTmEmCE

builderInsights.title: Nikunj Kothari
builderInsights.suggestedSummary:
Been tinkering with a “Home” @NousResearch agent for a few months and it’s finally gotten really good..

It’s also our first “group” bot where my wife and I interact with it on a daily basis - which has been fun learning especially when it fails 😅.

I have tried to recreate with Grok Bot and similar and you can’t get this level of granularity and control (eg only read certain emails, convert in line attachments to structured data or logged in browser sessions)

I asked it to share what it does based on the capabilities and our conversations and you can see it’s response below!

Before she wakes up and corrects  me, she never “wanted” it in the first place.. 

We threatened to make Tiramisu and that’s when her preference spilled out. 

Sous chef had a great time eating half the batter 😂 https://t.co/QRRzY9dCpr

Wife wanted Black Forest cake for her birthday..

I haven’t baked in a long long time, so not perfect but think it turned out ok (thanks @ChatGPT)

Happy birthday @shimoleejhaveri - I love you mostest ❤️ https://t.co/5LC3blykHK

I use these 8 AI skills to produce my entire podcast while still applying my taste and judgment along the way.

1. /podcast-prep does research on the guest and then preps an interview guide.

2. /podcast-edit reviews the raw transcript, then works with me to pick engaging quotes for the intro reel along with moments to cut.

3. /podcast-production orchestrates 5 skills to turn the full episode into 6 different assets.

Some people think the latest models make skills redundant but they've been indispensable for me to get AI to follow my specific edit and browser-use instructions.

My latest video highlighting how I actually work with these skills is a good watch if you want to automate any manual workflow.

📌 Watch me demo all 8 skills here: https://t.co/PYNbe5tlFw
